description:
See the tables, sizes and relationships the engine would build, before any rows exist. Free (no
    rows are made), so it is worth calling before generate_dataset on anything non-trivial: review
    what it understood and assumed, then adjust your request or schema before spending a real call.

    Args:
        request: Plain-English description (needs an LLM key, unless `schema`/`ddl` is also given —
                 then it is still used to ground realism, e.g. locale and what columns mean).
        schema:  A Misata schema dict (see the server instructions for the format). No key needed for
                 structure.
        ddl:     CREATE TABLE statements. No key needed for structure.

    Returns:
        route:         "chat" (not a dataset request — see `reply`), "design" (the model designed the
                       tables) or "pack" (matched a built-in shape).
        tables:        name, estimated rows, columns, foreign keys for each table the engine would build.
        understanding: what the engine read the request as (business, archetype, assumptions).
        requirements:  every specific thing the request asked for, so you can see what was understood.
        With a schema or ddl, also: numbers (each stated number it read), window, as_of (the data's last day),
        rows (each table's size), planned (the sizes the numbers set, with why), held and set_aside (each
        number the build will hold, or set aside with the reason).
        over_cap:      with a schema or ddl whose sizes pass this connection's row cap, that generate_dataset refuses it
                       and how to size it under the cap.
        cannot_hold:   numbers the request states that no rows can hold together (a rate past 100%, parts adding up
                       past their whole), each in plain words with what to write instead; generate_dataset refuses
                       the request as written until they are changed (say_so_plainly says so).
name: plan_dataset
title: Plan a dataset
